messages.content: i went to buy a new cup, but came home without one. i saw many i liked, but i did not need any of them.
it sounds like you enjoyed looking and still chose to leave without buying. did that feel like a clear choice when you made it?
yes. i have enough cups. i just liked seeing the different color and shape.
you can enjoy looking at things without having to take one home. you can like an object and still choose not to buy it.
can you help me tell my sister without making it sound like i could not choose?
i saw many cups i liked, but i already have enough. i chose not to buy one today.
use a few instead of many.
i saw a few cups i liked, but i already have enough. i chose not to buy one today.
why is chose not to buy different from could not buy?
chose not to buy says it was your choice. could not buy would give the idea that something kept you from buying, such as not having enough money.
only give the sentence about my choice.
i chose not to buy one today.
now add that i enjoyed looking.
i enjoyed looking at the cups and chose not to buy one today.
what is the difference between if my brother comes and when my brother comes?
if leaves open whether he will come. when often starts from the idea that he will come and talks about that time or what happens then.
make that explanation shorter.
if leaves open whether he will come. when often starts from the idea that he will come and talks about that time.
give a full sentence with each.
if my brother comes, we can read together. when my brother comes, we will read together.
does the first sentence say for sure that he is coming?
no. it gives what you can do if he comes, while leaving open whether he will come.
what if i know he cannot come today?
then do not use the sentence as a real plan for today. you could say: my brother cannot come today, so we will read together another day.
i do not know another day yet. leave that open too.
my brother cannot come today. i hope we can read together another day.
now just give the first if sentence again.
if my brother comes, we can read together.
can i use it in a made up story even if he is not really coming?
yes. just keep clear that the story is made up, rather than a real plan.
write a longer story about a child finding a picture of a house and asking where it is. use no place name.

a child found a picture of a small house between the pages of an old book. he showed it to his grandmother and asked whether it was her house. she looked at the front, then turned it over. on the back was a short message from her brother saying that he had stayed there during a holiday. the child had thought the picture was about his grandmother because it was in her book. now he knew she had kept it because her brother had sent it. she told him about her brother and the messages they used to send. the house in the picture was part of that story, but it was not where she had lived.
why did he first think it might be her house?
he found the picture in her book and thought that might mean the house was hers.
what changed his understanding?
the message on the back said that her brother had stayed there during a holiday.
did turning the picture change the house?
no. it gave him more information about the same picture.
what could he ask to learn why she kept it?
why did you keep this picture in your book?
answer in her voice using the story.
i kept it because my brother sent it to me. it helps me remember the messages we used to share.
can you know the name of the town from this?
no. the story gives no town name. the house is part of the made up story, not a place we can name from these details.
finish with him putting it back.
he put the picture between the pages again. now he knew there was a message on the other side.
my message is i will be at the library after lunch. change after lunch to before lunch. only give the new message.
i will be at the library before lunch.
now make it about my sister instead of me.
my sister will be at the library before lunch.
only tell me how to change the person in that sentence.
change i to my sister.
now give that as a full sentence about what i can do.
you can change i to my sister.
why did you keep before lunch the same?
you asked to change the person, not the time. the new sentence should keep the time unless you ask to change it too.
now keep my sister and change library to market.
my sister will be at the market before lunch.
ask it as a question instead.
will my sister be at the market before lunch?
can you answer that real question from the writing task alone?
not as a fact about your sister. we changed an example sentence. that does not tell me her real plan.
i have four containers on the table. two have rice and one has bread. can you know what is in the last one?
not from that information alone. you gave what was inside three containers, but not the last one.
could it be empty?
yes. it could be empty, but it could also hold something else. we do not know yet.
now i say it is empty. how many containers have food?
three containers have food.
if i move the bread into one of the rice containers, how many have food now?
then two containers have food, if all the bread is moved out and nothing else changes.
give that explanation in fewer words.
two have food if all the bread was moved and nothing else changed.
how many containers are on the table?
still four, unless you moved one off the table. moving the food does not itself move the container.
i take away both empty containers now.
then two containers are left on the table, and both have food.
only give how many are left.
two containers.
i want to tell my friend i am cleaning my room today. i am not asking them to help.
you can simply say: i am cleaning my room today. that gives your plan without making a request.
what if they answer do you need help?
then you can thank them and say whether you want help. if you do not, say that clearly and in a kind way.
write a no that says i am okay doing it myself.
thank you for asking. i am okay doing it myself today.
can i ask to talk later without making it sound like they need to wait all day?
you can say you would like to talk later and ask whether they want a message when you are done. that leaves them free to do their own things.
write that as a short question.
would you like me to send a message when i am done, so we can see if it is a good time to talk?
can you make it shorter?
may i send you a message when i am done?
does that say for sure that we will talk right away?
no. it asks about sending a message. you would still need to know whether both of you are free to talk then.
only give the first sentence about the room again.
i am cleaning my room today.
write a story about two friends choosing where to sit. one likes the window and one likes the quiet part of the room.

two friends came to the library to read together. one wanted to sit near the window, while the other wanted the quiet part away from the door. at first, they talked as if they had to choose between light and quiet. then they walked around the room. there was a small table near a window at the back, far from the door. they sat there and opened their books. neither had needed to give up the whole thing they wanted. looking at the room had given them a choice that their first conversation had not given.
what did each friend want?
one wanted to sit near the window. the other wanted a quiet place away from the door.
why was looking useful?
it gave them information about the real room. there was a place with both things they wanted.
can every pair of things people want always work together like that?
no. this story has a place that works for both. in another room, they might need a different choice or let one person choose this time and the other person choose next time.
write a question one friend could ask before saying no to the other.
is there a place near a window that is also quiet?
what if all the window places are busy?
then they can choose another place or wait. how much time they have may help them choose.
make that explanation shorter.
they can wait or choose another place, using the time they have.
finish with them reading, without a rule at the end.
one put a cup next to the book, and the other moved a chair near the table. they read quietly until it was time to go.
is she has to go the same as she wants to go?
no. has to go says there is a need or rule for her to go. wants to go says going is what she wants.
can both be true?
yes. she may need to go and also want to go.
can she have to go even if she does not want to?
yes. she could say: i have to go, but i would rather stay here.
now make it about me. i want to go, but there is no need for me to go.
i want to go, but i do not have to.
why is do in do not have to?
do helps make the sentence with not. use i do not have to go when you mean there is no need for you to go.
only give that correct sentence now.
i do not have to go.
does not have to mean must not?
no. do not have to leaves the choice open. must not gives a rule that says not to do it.
explain that again with need in the first part.
do not have to says there is no need. must not gives a rule that says not to do it.
